f370.summary: Henri IV to Maisse, his ambassador at Venice: Cardinal de Gondi has passed near Venice and the marquis de Pisany follows him to the Pope for the Catholic royalists, so Maisse must stay at his post; Lambert returns to the Levant with the despatch for Brèves, which Maisse may amend; the King approves Maisse's warnings to the English ambassador and Brèves; the King of Spain's ambition; Lesdiguières's war in Piedmont and the help the Italian friends should give; the Pope's resolutions are awaited. The whole cipher passage is transcribed group by group and aligned with the contemporary Brienne 13 copy (97.6% letter agreement).
f370.en:
Cardinal de Gondi will have passed near you, some days ago already; he will have told you my news and the state in
which he left things here, and that he would soon be followed by the marquis de Pisany, who is going to the Pope in the
name of the Catholics of this kingdom who serve me. I believe this will have made you change your decision to leave
and come home, as your last letter showed you meant to do; for you have judged well enough that at this juncture my
affairs over there must not be left without your presence, and I am so sure of your devotion to my service that you
would not want to fail me at the moment when your staying there is most necessary and useful. The continual
difficulties that attend my affairs have not allowed the said marquis to leave as soon as I would have wished:

f373.summary: Henri IV acknowledges Maisse's letter of 4 October and will wait for the outcome of the Gondi and Pisany mission; urges the Venetian friends to help him with money and to work on the Pope, since only his person can preserve the Crown; approves Maisse's handling of the third-party (tiers parti) rumour; the duc de Retz has left without funding the Swiss, the League expects reinforcements while Parma is ill; Lesdiguières must be supported in Piedmont; Brèves has the Levant charge and Maisse is asked to stay at Venice a little longer. A clear postscript announces Joyeuse's defeat and death before Villemur.
f373.en:
Monsieur de Maisse, on the very day the last despatch I made to you left (its duplicate goes with this one), I received your letter of the fourth of last month, and have seen and well considered all the points in it, on which I was very glad that you set them out for me so particularly together with your advice on them, since that can help me a great deal to make up my mind in my affairs according to the reliance I can place on what may depend on the means and resolutions over there.

Although I think I must wait before making a final judgement, to know what comes of the journey of Cardinal de Gondi and the marquis de Pisany, in which I believe I have gone as far to satisfy what my Catholic friends and servants could want of me as reason and the present safety of my affairs allow.

system: Maisse's Cipher (1592): a simple substitution on a 22-letter alphabet in figures 1-22, with doubled-letter signs (66, 67, 68, 72, 73), a second sign (omega) for d and a sparse nomenclator above the band.
